issues.description: The problem statement and the template expect animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (used in the UML and in the commented example in Main.java), but the solution repository implements these as SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat instead. This name/type mismatch between expected class names and the solution's classes can confuse students (and automated graders) because Main.java and the UML refer to Seal/Pig/Goat, while the solution only provides Space-prefixed versions and leaves Goat.java, Pig.java, and Seal.java effectively empty.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename or provide the expected classes to match the specification: either (a) rename SpaceSeal/SpacePig/SpaceGoat to Seal/Pig/Goat in the solution, or (b) add concrete Seal, Pig, and Goat classes that implement the same behavior (possibly delegating to the Space* implementations). Ensure the template Main.java and the UML refer to the same class names provided in the solution so students and tests are not confused by differing type names.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to concrete animal classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat (the UML and Main.java examples), but the solution implementation introduces classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat. This inconsistent naming for the same conceptual entities can confuse students: they may search for Seal/Pig/Goat in the solution or template and not find them, and automated/visual checks (or using getClass().getSimpleName() in the song) will produce different names than those shown in the exercise description.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the class names across artifacts. Either rename the solution classes to Seal, Pig, and Goat (e.g., SpaceSeal -> Seal) so they match the problem UML and template examples, or update the problem statement and template to consistently use the Space-prefixed names. Ensure tests and example code (Main.java) use the same class identifiers.
